text:

I’m an junior Engineering student at Harvey Mudd College specializing in mechatronics, with a Humanities, Social Sciences, and Arts concentration in Science, Technology, and Society. My work focuses on building reliable engineering solutions that prioritize the end user. My goal is to make Engineering solutions more accessible to everyone.
I thrive on solving physical problems through dynamic mechanical, electrical, and computer design, analytical modeling, rapid prototyping, and live troubleshooting.




Mechatronics: Integrating electronic sensors and actuators with mechanical design, and controlling them through embedded systems and firmware.
Control Systems: Utilizing feedback loops, characterizing system behaviour, predicting system outputs.
Human Centered Design: Prioritizing human needs through empathizing with users and understanding their problems.





To be honest, I consider all of the projects on this page as well as my on-campus jobs part of my hobbies, but outside of that…

Music: Composing and arranging music, playing in bands or solo (mainly trumpet and drum kit). I was in 4 bands at once in high school, I arranged compositions for us to play during concerts, and I’ve played all modern brass instruments!
Physical Activity: Competitive ball hockey (ice hockey but you run instead of skate), biking, hiking. I’ve played defence, forward, and goalie in the 4 years I represented my high school in ball hockey. In the year I played goalie, we had several shutouts and my team ranked 2nd in the Hong Kong International Schools Sports Federation!

Engineering a More Accessible World


I thrive on the challenge of translating complex human needs into functional, reliable engineering solutions. I am passionate about applying my skills to solve complex problems through intentional mechatronic design.




I’m a Junior Engineering student at Harvey Mudd College specializing in mechatronics. My academic work focuses on mechanics, digital and electronic systems, controls, and human-centred design.


Beyond the classroom, you can always find me tinkering with my personal projects - whether it’s building a new electromechanical device or improving upon my previous designs, I’m always on the move to build highly reliable, real-world products.
